findings.source_passage: Out of the trunk, the branches grow; out of them, the twigs. So, in productive subjects, grow the chapters.
findings.why_it_matters: This aphoristic opening is the chapter's most rhetorically distinctive sentence—a meta-commentary on the book's own structure that critics and readers cite as voice-establishing. Its complete absence removes Melville's self-reflexive digressive register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-sentence opening verbatim or near-verbatim as a prefatory line before the technical description begins.

findings.source_passage: as readily from its rest as a backwoodsman swings his rifle from the wall
findings.why_it_matters: This simile is a signature Melvillean move—grounding exotic whaling practice in a distinctly American frontier image. Its loss strips the passage of its rhetorical color and Americanist resonance.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the backwoodsman simile: 'as readily from its rest as a backwoodsman swings his rifle from the wall.'

findings.source_passage: this critical act is not always unattended with the saddest and most fatal casualties
findings.why_it_matters: This understated, ironic close to the paragraph—warning of fatal casualties through heavy litotes—is characteristic of Melville's deadpan narrative voice and carries foreshadowing weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clause preserving the litotic phrasing: 'this act is not always unattended with the most fatal casualties.'

summary: The draft competently compresses the technical content but loses the chapter's rhetorical frame (the trunk/branches aphorism) and one signature simile (the backwoodsman), constituting two medium findings and one low—below the regeneration threshold.
